note: Pipeline settings that are the same for every style: models, trimming, output format and the verification tolerances. Everything about how a style looks and sounds lives in styles/<style>.json.

transcribe.note: faster-whisper. Only the text and language are used; word timings come from forced alignment.

align.note: wav2vec2 CTC forced alignment of the transcript. One model frame is 20 ms; the alignment is repeated with the audio shifted by 1/phases of a frame and averaged, so timings do not depend on where the clip starts. Audio longer than chunk_s is run through the model in overlapping windows.

trim.note: The clip starts on the first frame at most lead_s before the first word and ends on the first frame at least tail_s after the last word ends (or at the end of the recording). With --start/--end only that window plus window_margin_s on each side is transcribed and aligned. The first caption's shutter must play in full: its biggest wave sits on the caption's first frame and its first click (its first sample within first_click_rel_db of the biggest wave: about 52 ms earlier at Prime's pitches) must come after the start of the video, so at 30 fps the first caption needs frame 2 or later. If it lands earlier (--start just before a word, or a clip-alignment a frame earlier than the source alignment), the trim start moves back by the missing frames, when the recording has them, and the move is logged (plan.json notes); the voice stays silent over those frames (clip.voice_start_frame) and fades in where it did, so nothing from before the requested start is heard, and the voice is aligned from where it starts (when planning and when verifying), so the timings do not depend on the move (Tears of Steel at --start 24: 'Tom', barely audible under the film's music, alignment score 0.04, landed anywhere from the first frame of the audio to its real start when the extra frames were aligned with it); otherwise the plan lists the problem and nothing is rendered (exit 2).

quality.note: Checked at the plan stage, before anything is rendered: Whisper's language probability (1.0 with --lang), the mean CTC score of the words aligned on the clip, and the largest difference between a word's start aligned on the source window and on the trimmed clip. If one is out of range the transcript or its timing is probably wrong (unclear speech, music, wrong language): plan.json is written with the problems listed and the CLI exits 2 without rendering. Check the words and their times in plan.json (or run again with --lang), then render it with --plan (a loaded plan is not re-checked for this). Measured: client's Dutch test clip 0.94 mean score and 5 ms; good English clip 0.67 and 12 ms; a misheard English clip ('I don't know.', language probability 0.55) 0.04 and 730 ms.

editing.note: PREFERENCES.md 'Editing' asks to cut pauses longer than ~0.3 s and hide each jump cut with a view switch, 1-2 negative frames and a flash sound. That rule came after the client approved Prime v11, which keeps its pauses, and the pipeline does not cut. Until the client decides, every pause longer than pause_s is listed in plan.json and report.json with pause_status.

output.note: Sources taller than wide become 1080x1920, others 1920x1080 (centre-cropped if the aspect differs). bt709 SDR in, bt709 out.

verify.note: caption_lead_frames: each caption's first frame (detected in the final frames, compared at 1/detect_scale size against the clean clip with each caption within detect_neighbours frames; a caption that looks exactly like the one before it has no visible change and keeps its planned frame) comes 0-2 frames before its first word, +- align_tolerance_s (one CTC frame), with the words re-aligned on the clean voice track of the final timeline (client rule: effects in the mix pull the aligner by up to ~100 ms). shutter_*: each caption's own shutter (rebuilt alone at its planned pitch, level and pan, its biggest wave on the caption frame) is cross-correlated, both high-passed above shutter_highpass_hz so the hit's low end does not pull it, with the effects part of the final over lags up to +-shutter_max_lag_s (well under the min_frames spacing of the captions, so a neighbouring caption's shutter cannot be picked up); the lag is the offset of the biggest wave and must be within shutter_tolerance_ms, the normalised correlation at least shutter_min_correlation, and the shutter's level in the final relative to the plan within shutter_level_range. Every caption is on screen for at least the style's grouping.min_frames frames, measured on the caption changes found in the final frames. The effects part of the final (final minus the voice rebuilt through the same limiter) must match the effects track (correlation >= effects_min_correlation). In the track, a sound starts where the level above onset_highpass_hz (RMS over onset_rms_s, every onset_hop_s; 500 Hz keeps out the hit's sub-bass and the flutter of its low reverb tail, which read as new sounds when a final hit rings out fully) rises onset_rise_db above its level onset_before_s earlier, above onset_floor_db re its loudest moment; every onset must lie within allowed_onset_s of a caption frame (the shutter's clicks run from about -55 to +30 ms). Between those windows the level (RMS over fade_rms_s) may not rise more than fade_rise_db above its running minimum (above fade_floor_db): sounds only fade there. edge_*: the final audio in its first and last edge_window_s (either channel) stays below edge_max_dbfs, so the video starts and ends in silence and loops without a tick. Placement: the style must ask for centre placement, every caption layer's ink box (every pixel it inks, faint hairlines included) must be centred on the frame within half a pixel, and in every captioned final frame the caption layer, composited on the clean clip frame like the final (zoom included) at each shift within +-placement_search_px, must fit the final frame best at a shift within centre_tolerance_px of none; a frame counts as measured when the caption at that shift explains it at least placement_min_fit times better (squared error) than no caption (about 1 where a difference-blend caption cannot be seen, over mid grey; 70-2500 on the test clips). The box of the visibly changed pixels is not used for placement: the thin, low-alpha hairlines of a lopsided script word ('Passions', 'Space') vanish in it and a centred word measured up to 7.5 px off. Blend: in each captioned frame the ink is every pixel that differs from the clean clip frame (zoomed like the final) by more than ink_threshold (0-255, any channel); of those, at least blend_min_match (per caption) must match the Difference blend |C - B| within blend_tolerance, and more of them than match a normal blend (C). Sound onsets are measured with silence before t = 0, so a sound already playing on the first sample is found; every shutter must be complete, its first click (trim.first_click_rel_db) inside the video.
